stemMd: A campaign says, “Either we build a large car park in the square or the town centre will lose all visitors.” What should be questioned first?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Whether other ways of maintaining visitor access have been excluded without justification.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Whether every building has the same height.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Whether visitors can count parking spaces.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whether the square has a name.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Whether the word visitors is plural.

explanationMd: The argument presents only two outcomes as if they exhaust the possibilities. Other access measures, smaller interventions or existing transport might preserve visits. The first issue is the unsupported exclusion of alternatives, not whether a car park could have any benefit.

distractorRationale.d: Naming does not affect the range of access alternatives.
distractorRationale.c: This does not address the forced choice.
distractorRationale.b: Building height is irrelevant to the stated dilemma.
distractorRationale.e: Grammar does not identify the substantive reasoning problem.
